locator: The whole print; a woman in a maid's cap and white apron stands behind an ironing board, centre. Her face, frontal, is at x 535-665, y 445-590 of the 1205 x 1536 file: about 130 px across and 145 px hairline to chin.
rights_note: The Library of Congress states 'No known restrictions on publication.' A photograph copyrighted in 1908 is in the public domain in the United States.
access_notes: Found 2026-11-07 through loc.gov searches (photos, 'domestic servants', dates 1890-1912); record and master TIFF fetched from loc.gov and tile.loc.gov with curl. The record notes: 'This record contains unverified, old data from caption card'; tracings 'Electricity 1908; Ads Household appliances...; Household appliances...; Electricity; Domestic servants; Adv.; Shelf.' Other places tried: the LOC stereograph comedies of maids ('Bridget' series, Standard Scenic Co. 1906; E.W. Kelley 1904-1907) - faces 40-90 px and staged comic types; Frances Benjamin Johnston's Lynn shoe-factory women, c1895 (factory workers, faces small or downcast); Detroit Publishing 'The house maid' (a reproduction of a William McGregor Paxton painting, not a photograph). The Met's open-access search returned no public-domain maid photographs; Smithsonian, Minnesota and Wisconsin Historical Society were not searched in this pass.
note: THIS IS NOT MARY REYNOLDS. No photograph of Mary Reynolds was found. This woman stands in for her because she is an American woman photographed in 1908, within four years of the scene, dressed as a house maid (white cap, high-collared white shirtwaist, apron), and Mary Reynolds was the Glessners' house maid in 1900 (born June 1871 in Illinois; 33 in 1904). The LC caption calls her a 'house maid' but the photograph is a General Electric advertising picture, so she may be a model posed as a maid rather than a working servant. She is not named; her age, birthplace and ancestry are not recorded. By appearance she is in her twenties, younger than Mary Reynolds; nothing in the record says she is Irish-American (Reynolds is only a surname). A studio advertising photograph against a dark backdrop, with 'General Electric Company, Schenectady, New York.' printed across the top. A young woman stands behind an ironing board pressing a lace doily with an electric iron, its cord hanging from a ceiling fitting at left. She wears a white frilled maid's cap pinned on top of full, dark, centre-parted hair drawn up and back; a white high-collared shirtwaist with full sleeves and a dark bow tie; a white apron. Her face is frontal, looking at the camera with a broad open smile: an oval face, straight dark brows, dark eyes, a straight nose, a rounded chin. The smile widens the cheeks and mouth; a neutral face would read narrower in the lower half. The scan is a copy negative of a print, soft at this scale.
what_it_supplies: the proportions of a young American woman's face in the scene's decade, frontal
how a house maid's cap, shirtwaist, bow and apron looked about 1908, as an advertiser presented them
